question.leadin: The 7th pope by of this name attacked simony and tried to strengthen papal authority in his namesake reforms starting around 1050-1080.
question.text: Identify this name shared by several popes, the 13th of whom is best remembered for his calendar reforms.
question.clue: Henry IV walked to Canossa in a hair shirt to have an excommunication that was given to him by a pope of this name rescinded during the Investiture Controversy.

swap.text: The papal bull Ineffabilis Deus was issued by this pope. He held the longest reign of any Catholic pope, 32 years, and also convened the First Vatican Council.
swap.clue: His encyclical Ubi Primum defined the doctrine of the Immaculate Conception.

question.text: Name this rival Order, which had possessions famously confiscated by the French king Philip and Pope Clement V.
question.clue: At the Battle of Montgisard, they helped defeat Saladin's army, and they were founded after the First Crusade by Hugues de Payens and Godfrey de Saint-Omer to protect pilgrims traveling to the Holy Land.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Mexican Constitution of 1857.
swap.text: The constitution weakened the influence of this church, whose members later revolted in the Cristero War. This Christian denomination was the official religion of Mexico's former colonizer, Spain.
swap.clue: This institution was stripped of property by the Lerdo Law, which was opposed by Conservative leader Felix Zuloaga during the Reform War in Mexico.

question.leadin: Pope Martin V was elected following this ecumenical council, which also condemned Jan Hus as a heretic.
question.text: Name this 15th century council, which ended the Western Schism.
question.clue: This event saw the order to exhume the bones of John Wycliffe and occurred due to the wishes of Emperor Sigismund.

swap.text: Pope Leo X listed 41 errors he had found in Luther's Theses and his other works in this Papal Bull, which gave Luther 60 days to retract those errors.
swap.clue: Some of the specific claims this document notes as especially problematic include: "A good work very well done is a venial sin," and "Christians must be taught to cherish excommunications rather than to fear them."

question.leadin: Answer these questions about ecumenical councils.
question.text: This council established the Primacy of St. Peter over the other apostles and laid the groundwork for the doctrine of papal infallibility. The pope who called it also penned the Syllabus of Errors.
question.answerHtml: First Vatican Council [or Vatican I; prompt “Vatican” alone; do NOT accept “Vatican II” or “Second Vatican”] <SSp>
question.clue: This meeting declared anathema on anyone who disbelieved in miracles, condemned all opposition to Ultramontanism, and enacted several principles first put forth in the Syllabus of Errors.

swap.text: This pope was also a Medici. During his papacy, Rome was sacked in 1527 and Henry VIII of England created the Anglican church.
swap.clue: His imprisonment in the Castel Sant'Angelo helped lead to the election of Niccolo Capponi as Gonfaloniere of the Florentine Republic.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Sebastianism, the belief that King Sebastian of Portugal will return to aid his country in its time of need.
question.text: In 1759, the Marquis of Pombal used the Tavora Affair to justify his persecution of Sebastianists and this group. This group was officially suppressed in the Papal Bull Dominus ac Redemptor.
question.clue: Two members of this group prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk and another created a lunisolar calendar for the last Ming emperor.

swap.text: In 1997 this Polish pope bestowed Romero with the title Servant of God. This pope's reign from 1978 to his death in 2005 is the 3rd longest in history.
swap.answerHtml: Pope John Paul II [or Karol Józef Wojtyła; accept JP2; prompt on Pope John Paul]
swap.clue: This man made a prison visit to forgive Mehmet Ali Agca, a member of the Grey Wolves who tried to kill him.

question.leadin: Stuff about the Great Schism in the Catholic Church.
question.text: The conflict originated in the Babylonian Captivity, in which Philip IV moved the papacy to this French city and appointed Clement V as pope.
question.clue: This city was called "a sewer where all the muck of the universe collects" by Petrarch, who coined an enduring Biblical nickname for it.

swap.leadin: This doctrine was pronounced by the papal constitution Ineffabilis Deus on December 8th, 1854.
swap.text: Name this doctrine stating that the Virgin Mary was "preserved exempt from all stain of original sin."
swap.clue: That bull, Ineffabilis Deus, was issued on the day of the "Feast" of this doctrine - December 8th - by Pope Pius IV.

question.text: At the end of the Wars of Castro, this pope ordered the city of Castro razed after blaming Ranuccio II for the death of a bishop he appointed. He opposed the terms of the Peace of Westphalia.
question.clue: Originally, he was elected as a compromise against the candidate put forth by Mazarin, with whom he bickered almost continuously for the eleven-year duration of his papacy.

swap.leadin: This pope allowed Teresa of Avila to found her own branch of the Discalced Carmelites, who went by the amusing acronym O.C.D.
swap.text: Name this pope, who employed Aloysius Lilius and Christopher Clavius to create a system that was implemented by the bull Inter gravissimas.
swap.clue: Born Ugo Buoncompagni (bone-comp-AHN-yee), he proposed the deposition of Queen Elizabeth I but left a more lasting impact with his namesake calendar.

question.leadin: This organization divided its territories into langues ("LAHNG") whose administration was organized by nationality.
question.text: Name this organization that was forced from Rhodes after an Ottoman siege. This organization was led during that siege by Philippe Villiers de L'Isle-Adam ("vill-ee-YAY de LEEL uh-DAHM").
question.answerHtml: Knights Hospitaller [or Order of Hospitallers; accept Order of Knights of the Hospital of Saint John in Jerusalem or Knights of Saint John or Order of Saint John; accept Knights of Malta; prompt on Knights of Rhodes]
question.clue: This group, founded by the Blessed Gerard, controlled the fortresses of Margat (mar-GAH) and Krak des Chevaliers ("crack" deh sheh-val-YAY) before it was forced from the Holy Land.

swap.leadin: An attempt to end this period at the conciliabolo, or "secret meeting," ended up creating a third faction by electing Alexander V.
swap.text: Name this period in which two, then three, people simultaneously laid claim to the papacy. The 1409 Council of Pisa failed to end this period.
swap.answerHtml: Western Schism [accept Schism of 1378; accept Papal Schism; accept Great Occidental Schism]
swap.clue: Pierre d'Ailly ("dah-YEE") and Jean Gerson ("zhawn zhair-SON") promoted a conciliar resolution to this conflict, which began when 13 rebels staged an election in Fondi ("FOHN-dee") with regalia stolen by a camerlengo.

question.leadin: Answer the following about some gender-bending historical times.
question.text: Notable events in the history of this period saw John X made to watch the execution of his brother Peter by Maria, daughter of Theodora the Elder. Earlier, Theodora allegedly sired John XI with Sergius III.
question.answerHtml: The Pornocracy [or Saeculum Obscurum or The Rule of the Harlets or Hurenregiment]
question.clue: In addition to John X, this period saw the reign of Lando, and much of the information known about this period comes from the writings of Liutprand of Cremona.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about syncretic misadventures in Asia.
swap.text: This term refers to a controversy in the 17th and 18th centuries, mostly between Jesuits and Dominicans, over whether ancestor worship should be allowed in a certain country's practice of Christianity. A bull issued by Pope Clement XI in 1715
swap.answerHtml: the <u>Chinese Rites</u> controversy [don’t accept other answers, this is a fairly discrete term]

question.leadin: This term has been used by Martin Luther and several others to describe the Avignon papacy.
question.text: Identify this term which refers to an event that occurred during the reign of Nebuchadnezzar.
question.clue: This period in which Philip IV of France moved the Papacy to Avignon, named after a duration of time in the Old Testament.

swap.leadin: This pope convened the Fifth Lateran Council, during which he condemned the Pragmatic Sanction of Charles VII of France.
swap.text: Identify this "Warrior Pope", who rose to power by convincing Cesare Borgia to support him in the Papal Conclave. He was also the patron of Michelangelo, whom he ordered to paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
swap.clue: Louis XII convened a conciliabulum at Pisa against this ruler, though earlier this ruler had allied with France, Spain, and the Holy Roman Empire against Venice, forming the League of Cambrai.
